web.title: Matar Chhilo: Kitty Party Game Rules, How to Play and Twists
web.description: Matar Chhilo is a winter kitty party race where ladies shell fresh peas in 2 minutes and freeze on "Saas aayi!". Learn what you need, rules and fun twists.
web.intro: Matar Chhilo is a winter kitty party game where every lady gets a heap of fresh pea pods and races to shell as many matar dane as she can into her katori in 2 minutes. The lady with the most teaspoons of peas when the timer ends wins. The crazy twist: whenever the host shouts "Saas aayi!", everyone must drop the pods, join hands and say "Namaste mummyji!", and anyone caught still shelling tips 5 dane into her neighbour's katori. Nothing is wasted, because all the peas go into one patila for the host's matar paneer.
materials: About 250 g of fresh green pea pods per lady
One empty steel katori per lady
Old newspaper sheets to catch the peels
A phone timer set to 2 minutes
One teaspoon for the host to count the peas
One big patila or bowl to collect all the peas at the end
steps: Seat everyone around a table or on the floor. Put a newspaper sheet, a heap of about 250 g of pea pods and an empty steel katori in front of each lady.
The host starts a 2 minute timer and every lady shells as fast as she can, peas into her katori and peels onto the newspaper.
Two or three times during the 2 minutes the host shouts "Saas aayi!". Everyone must stop at once, join hands in namaste and say "Namaste mummyji!" before going back to shelling.
Any lady the host catches still shelling after "Saas aayi!" must tip 5 peas from her katori into the katori of the lady on her right.

When the timer ends, all hands off. The host counts each katori with a teaspoon, and the most teaspoons wins. Then every lady pours her peas into one patila for the host to cook matar paneer or matar pulao.
rules: A peel or pod that falls into the katori must come out, or that teaspoon does not count.
Anyone still shelling after "Saas aayi!" gives 5 peas to the lady on her right.
Peas shelled after the timer ends do not count.
The host counts by level teaspoons, and the most teaspoons wins.
All peas are collected and cooked, so nothing goes to waste.
variations: In the final, every lady shells wearing woolen gloves.
Add a "Pati ka phone!" call where everyone holds a pea pod to her ear and says "Haan ji, haan ji!" before carrying on.
Shout "Saas aayi!" three times in the last 30 seconds for a chaotic finish.
tips: Buy the peas on the morning of the kitty so the pods are fresh and easy to open.
Weigh or count out the same amount for every lady so the race is fair.
Keep a dustbin bag ready to roll up the newspapers and peels at the end.
Tell the ladies before the kitty that the peas are for dinner, so everyone shells carefully.

faq.q: How many players do you need for Matar Chhilo?
faq.a: It works for 8 to 20 ladies, all playing at the same time. You only need enough pea pods and katoris for everyone.

faq.q: What do you need to play Matar Chhilo?
faq.a: About 250 g of fresh pea pods and one steel katori per lady, newspaper for the peels, a phone timer, a teaspoon for counting and one big patila for the peas.

faq.q: How long does the Matar Chhilo game take?
faq.a: Each race is just 2 minutes. With counting, a final round and collecting the peas, the game takes 10 to 15 minutes.
No. All the shelled peas go into one patila and the host cooks them, for example as matar paneer or matar pulao.

faq.q: Is Matar Chhilo a good winter kitty party game?
faq.a: Yes. Fresh matar is in every sabzi market in winter, the game needs no prep, and the "Saas aayi!" twist keeps the whole room laughing.
